messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered — control-plane 5xx spike observed across auth and org-lookup (us-east-1). Alerts: 5xx rate from gateway increased from ~0.2% to 8% in last 2m. Auto-escalation to #incidents.
lee: oncall here, looking now. Any immediate customer reports?
alex: seeing `502` and `504` in logs, many from config-service dependency timeouts. stacktrace snippets show `org-lookup` errors.
jordan: I can repro locally hitting `GET /v1/orgs/<id>` against staging-config -> latency is 1.2s but prod shows 7-12s then 5xx.
maya: metrics: auth 5xx spike started at 1953456680, p95 latency jumped from 120ms -> 1.8s. Related errors: downstream `billing-lookup` returning 500 for a subset.
samir: @lee paging ops team: can we scale replicas for auth and org-lookup in us-east-1? Could be overload or a broken cache.
lee: scaling auth + org-lookup now (k8s). `kubectl scale deploy/auth --replicas=6 -n prod-us-east` and `kubectl scale deploy/org-lookup --replicas=5 -n prod-us-east`.
ops-bot: Scaling commands executed: auth -> 6 replicas, org-lookup -> 5 replicas.
alex: rolling logs show increased 429 from config-gateway -> maybe rate-limited to config service. Recent config push at 1953456500? Anyone did a config rollout?
jordan: I rolled a small config change at ~1953456460 for feature flags — it touched config-service. Reverting now.
lee: rollback initiated for config-service: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/config-service -n prod-us-east`. Watch for errors.
maya: I put a temporary fallback in the gateway to skip org-lookup for known cached customers (cheap short-circuit). Patching routing rule now.
samir: quick healthcheck: `curl -sS -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null https://us-east.gateway.redwood/api/health` -> getting `502 1.03` repeatedly.
alex: digging into gateway logs: `error: upstream responded with 502 Bad Gateway: connection reset by peer` pointing at `config-service:443` and `org-lookup:443`.
lee: good. If rollback + scaling doesn't stabilize in 3m we'll flip route to cached=on for 100% for us-east (degrade recent behavior but maintain availability).
jordan: rollback completed on config-service, current rollout status: `deployment "config-service" successfully rolled back`.
ops-bot: Notifying on-call infra for possible network flapping between clusters.
maya: after rollback, error rate dipped from 8% -> 3% in ~90s. Still above baseline. P95 latency down to 420ms.
samir: running a forced cache warm for org-lookup: `POST /internal/orgs/_warm?scope=hot` against cache layer -> queued background job.
alex: also discovered a backlog in billing-lookup queue causing timeouts; clearing backlog worker pool and increasing concurrency to 12.
lee: ok we're seeing steady improvement. 5xx now at 0.8% and trending down. Any customer-facing incidents opened?
maya: Opened incident ticket INC-19534 and notified CS. Sent templated message to customers with degraded API errors and ETA: investigation ongoing.
jordan: quick test: synthetic user flows for create+lookup succeed; gateway 200 rate back to ~98.5% good.
samir: monitoring alert thresholds: reduce noisy alerts for a bit. Putting alert policy to warning for org-lookup for 30m.
lee: summary for paging: root cause suspected config-service rollout that increased latency and caused cascading timeouts to org-lookup and billing-lookup. Contributing factor: a hot cache churn and insufficient concurrency on billing workers.
alex: mitigation actions performed: rollback config-service, scaled auth/org-lookup, increased billing worker concurrency, warmed caches, applied short-circuit fallback on gateway.
maya: impact assessment: peak window 1953456680-1953456920 — ~7.3% of control-plane requests returned 5xx; about 1.1k customer API errors across 120 unique API keys. No SSO credentials compromised. We identified 3 enterprise customers with higher error rates; CS notified.
lee: moving to monitoring/observability handoff: ensure logs retained + add trace sampling for the next 24h. @alex can you own the traces?
alex: got it, I will keep traces and set a regression alert for similar latency pattern.
samir: postmortem owner? I'd like to volunteer. Will collect timeline, metrics, and actions.
maya: I'm taking customer comms + RCA writeup with samir.
lee: great. Closing pager in 10m if stability persists. Last check: current 5xx = 0.4% p95 latency = 130ms.
ops-bot: All monitored services in us-east reporting nominal.
lee: closing pager — follow-ups: postmortem, update deploy checklist to include cache-warm for config rollouts, add runbook step to scale billing workers proactively when p95 > 500ms.
jordan: noted. Will add runbook PR.
samir: I'll start the postmortem draft and link metrics/graphs.
maya: thanks team — good work. :thumbsup: 
lee: thanks — handing off to next on-call.
lee: incident resolved — monitoring for 30m.
